2255:     acc_cost_mat = numpy.full((l1 + 1, l2 + 1), 0)
2256: 
2257:     for i in range(1, l1 + 1):
2258:         for j in range(1, l2 + 1):
2259:             if numpy.isfinite(mask[i - 1, j - 1]):
2260:                 if numpy.sqrt(_njit_local_squared_dist(s1[i - 1], s2[j - 1])) <= eps:
2261:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = 1 + acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j - 1]
2262:                 else:
2263:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = max(
2264:                         acc_cost_mat[i][j - 1], acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j]
2265:                     )
2266: 
2267:     return acc_cost_mat
2268: 
2269: 
2270: def lcss_accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, eps, mask, be=None):
2271:     """Compute the longest common subsequence similarity score between
2272:     two time series.
2273: 
2274:     Parameters
2275:     ----------
2276:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,)
2277:         First time series. If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
2278:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,)
2279:         Second time series. If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
2280:     eps : float
2281:         Matching threshold.
2282:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2283:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
2284:     be : Backend object or string or None
2285:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
2286:         the NumPy backend is used.
2287:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
2288:         the PyTorch backend is used.
2289:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
2290:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
2291: 
2292:     Returns
2293:     -------
2294:     acc_cost_mat : array-like, shape=(sz1 + 1, sz2 + 1)
2295:         Accumulated cost matrix.
2296:     """
2297:     be = instantiate_backend(be, s1, s2)
2298:     s1 = to_time_series(s1, remove_nans=True, be=be)
2299:     s2 = to_time_series(s2, remove_nans=True, be=be)
2300:     l1 = be.shape(s1)[0]
2301:     l2 = be.shape(s2)[0]
2302:     acc_cost_mat = be.full((l1 + 1, l2 + 1), 0)
2303: 
2304:     for i in range(1, l1 + 1):
2305:         for j in range(1, l2 + 1):
2306:             if mask[i - 1, j - 1]:
2307:                 if be.is_numpy:
2308:                     squared_dist = _njit_local_squared_dist(s1[i - 1], s2[j - 1])
2309:                 else:
2310:                     squared_dist = _local_squared_dist(s1[i - 1], s2[j - 1], be=be)
2311:                 if be.sqrt(squared_dist) <= eps:
2312:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = 1 + acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j - 1]
2313:                 else:
2314:                     acc_cost_mat[i][j] = max(
2315:                         acc_cost_mat[i][j - 1], acc_cost_mat[i - 1][j]
2316:                     )
2317: 
2318:     return acc_cost_mat
2319: 
2320: 
2321: @njit(nogil=True)
2322: def _njit_lcss(s1, s2, eps, mask):
2323:     """Compute the longest common subsequence score between two time series.
2324: 
2325:     Parameters
2326:     ----------
2327:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d)
2328:         First time series.
2329:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d)
2330:         Second time series.
2331:     eps : float (default: 1.)
2332:         Maximum matching distance threshold.
2333:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2334:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
2335: 
2336:     Returns
2337:     -------
2338:     lcss_score : float
2339:         Longest Common Subsquence score between both time series.
2340:     """
2341:     l1 = s1.shape[0]
2342:     l2 = s2.shape[0]
2343:     acc_cost_mat = njit_lcss_accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, eps, mask)
2344: 
2345:     return float(acc_cost_mat[-1][-1]) / min([l1, l2])
2346: 
2347: 
2348: def _lcss(s1, s2, eps, mask, be=None):
2349:     """Compute the longest common subsequence score between two time series.
2350: 
2351:     Parameters
2352:     ----------
2353:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,)
2354:         First time series. If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
2355:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,)
2356:         Second time series. If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
2357:     eps : float (default: 1.)
2358:         Maximum matching distance threshold.
2359:     mask : array-like, shape=(sz1, sz2)
2360:         Mask. Unconsidered cells must have False values.
2361:     be : Backend object or string or None
2362:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
2363:         the NumPy backend is used.
2364:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
2365:         the PyTorch backend is used.
2366:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
2367:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
2368: 
2369:     Returns
2370:     -------
2371:     lcss_score : float
2372:         Longest Common Subsquence score between both time series.
2373:     """
2374:     be = instantiate_backend(be, s1, s2)
2375:     s1 = be.array(s1)
2376:     s2 = be.array(s2)
2377:     l1 = be.shape(s1)[0]
2378:     l2 = be.shape(s2)[0]
2379:     acc_cost_mat = lcss_accumulated_matrix(s1, s2, eps, mask, be=be)
2380:     return float(acc_cost_mat[-1][-1]) / min([l1, l2])
2381: 
2382: 
2383: def lcss(
2384:     s1,
2385:     s2,
2386:     eps=1.0,
2387:     global_constraint=None,
2388:     sakoe_chiba_radius=None,
2389:     itakura_max_slope=None,
2390:     be=None,
2391: ):
2392:     r"""Compute the Longest Common Subsequence (LCSS) similarity measure
2393:     between (possibly multidimensional) time series and return the
2394:     similarity.
2395: 
2396:     LCSS is computed by matching indexes that are met up until the eps
2397:     threshold, so it leaves some points unmatched and focuses on the
2398:     similar parts of two sequences. The matching can occur even if the
2399:     time indexes are different. One can set additional constraints to the
2400:     set of acceptable paths: the Sakoe-Chiba band which is parametrized by a
2401:     radius or the Itakura parallelogram which is parametrized by a maximum slope.
2402:     Both these constraints consists in forcing paths to lie close
2403:     to the diagonal. To retrieve a meaningful similarity value from the
2404:     length of the longest common subsequence, the percentage of that value
2405:     regarding the length of the shortest time series is returned.
2406: 
2407:     According to this definition, the values returned by LCSS range from
2408:     0 to 1, the highest value taken when two time series fully match,
2409:     and vice-versa. It is not required that both time series share the
2410:     same size, but they must be the same dimension. LCSS was originally
